fields.title: Building Automated Finance Tools with Python
fields.content:
anaging finances in Nigeria can be complex with inflation and multiple income streams. That's why I decided to build Budget-Pilot, a personal expense tracker.

The Process:
Using Python and MySQL, I developed a system that:
Tracks every Naira spent in real-time.
Categorizes expenses automatically.
Visualizes monthly spending trends.

The Lesson:
The biggest challenge wasn't the code; it was the data structure. Moving from a beginner to an intermediate Python developer meant learning how to handle database relations efficiently.

fields.title: How I Got Locked In and Built 42 Python Projects in 60 Days
fields.content:
A lot of people think learning to code means watching endless tutorial videos and getting trapped in "tutorial hell."

When I started my Python journey, I wanted a different approach. I didn't want to just read code.
I wanted to ship it. So, I challenged myself to a strict daily execution sprint.

The result? I got completely locked in and built 42 unique, functional scripts and applications from scratch.

From Zero to Full-Stack FinTech
Instead of keeping a cluttered desktop of random scripts, I organized my journey into five progressive stages to track my growth day by day:

The Core Logic: I started with basic conditional formatting and terminal games (like Guess My Number and word puzzles).

Desktop Automation: I moved on to practical everyday tools, like text-based To-Do lists, countdown timers, and building my first GUIs with Tkinter.

Web Scripting: Next, I connected my scripts to the internet, building automated email senders, image downloaders, and live weather apps using external APIs.

Data Analytics: I focused on data handling, writing scripts to plot custom Bar, Line, Pie, and Scatter charts.

Advanced Finance Logic: By the end of the sprint, I was building complex financial application simulations, complete with interactive state logic and banking chatbots.

Build in Public
I’ve archived all 42 projects into a single, highly structured repository on my GitHub. Whether you are looking for simple terminal logic or intermediary automation tools to learn from, you can dig into the source code right now.

 Check out the full archive here: https://github.com/kenetworkltd-oss/60-Days-of-Python-
